title: If you can't explain something in simple terms, you don't understand it (2017)
why_read: A well-worn but genuinely useful idea about explanation and understanding, likely sparking a thoughtful discussion thread rather than new technical content.
analysis: This is a 2017 essay revisiting the Feynman-adjacent idea that true understanding shows up as the ability to explain something simply. It is not a technical paper or tool but a reflection piece likely to generate discussion about teaching, communication, and self-assessment of knowledge. The idea is popular and often repeated, so it offers little new to readers already familiar with it, though the comment thread may surface interesting counterexamples or nuance. Worth a quick read for the discussion rather than for new information.
